analysis.course_name: Extended Security Engineering and Cyber Security
analysis.overview: Introductory cybersecurity course on security engineering: designing, monitoring, and maintaining security against adversaries. Covers fundamental security ideas, case studies of failing systems, attacker mindset, cryptography, memory corruption, and web/binary attacks. Extended version of COMP6441 with additional applied technical material, including a self-directed security project. Topics change yearly to stay current. Taught alongside COMP6441, LAWS3040, and CRIM3040.

topics.title: Security Engineering Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Think like a security engineer and analyse systems that fail
Apply a security engineering approach to real-world scenarios considering cost, human factors, risk, and privacy
topics.source_evidence: Course description: fundamental ideas, thinking like an attacker, failing systems

topics.title: Cryptography
learning_outcomes: Apply fundamental cryptographic primitives and protocols to achieve desired properties
Explain weaknesses and appropriate use of cryptographic approaches
topics.source_evidence: CLO5: cryptographic primitives, protocols, weaknesses, appropriate use

topics.title: Memory Corruption and Exploitation
learning_outcomes: Explain the main classes of memory corruption vulnerabilities
Evaluate relative strengths and weaknesses of deployed countermeasures
topics.source_evidence: CLO8: memory corruption vulnerabilities and countermeasures

topics.title: Web and Binary Security Attacks
learning_outcomes: Successfully attack common vulnerabilities in web based systems and binaries
topics.source_evidence: CLO9: attack common vulnerabilities in web systems and binaries

topics.title: Cybersecurity in Context
subtopics: Related fields: safety science, psychology, cybercrime
learning_outcomes: Assess likely future trends and emerging risks from historical context and current developments
Explain cybersecurity's relationship to related fields including safety science, psychology, and cybercrime
topics.source_evidence: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3: trends, related fields, key decision factors

topics.title: Applied Security Project and Professional Skills
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate professional competencies including self-directed research, time management, and ethical behaviour
Apply information and work measures, randomness, and privacy to design solutions for real-world security problems
topics.source_evidence: Course aims 4-5; CLO4, CLO6: applied skills, professionalism, randomness

study_notes: Assumed knowledge: coding (ideally C) and low-level computing concepts such as memory implementation and function calling.
Pass requirement: final grade of at least 50%.
Late penalty: 5% per calendar day; work submitted after 5 days (120 hours) receives zero.
Exam permits no generative AI (including grammar tools); must be completed as a plain text file. Project and portfolio permit simple editing assistance only.
COMP6841 students attend Monday and Tuesday 11am-1pm lectures, the Wednesday 2pm-4pm session, and an allocated tutorial; lecture attendance is optional and recorded.
